items.title: Supreme Court flags gaps in FSSAI plan for red-hexagon warning labels on foods high in fat, sugar, salt
items.summary: The Supreme Court on September 10 flagged several gaps in the FSSAI’s proposal for hexagon shaped warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and fat [ 3S And Our Health Society v. Union of India & Anr. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran sought a timeline for introducing the labels and questioned the proposed two-phase rollout, particularly the plan to initially cover only products high in at least two of sugar, salt and fat rather than all products high in any one of these nutrients. The Bench gave the FSSAI 10 days to respond and posted the matter for further hearing on September 28. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) plea seeking the display of warning labels on packaged food items to indicate their salt, sugar and fat levels. During an earlier hearing, the Bench had criticised the FSSAI’s handling of the issue and questioned whether the regulator was bowing to corporate pressure instead of acting on a matter concerning public health, particularly the health of children. The FSSAI subsequently filed an affidavit dated August 28 proposing red-coloured hexagonal labels for products high in any two or more of added saturated fat, added sugar and salt. The proposed labels would state “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR”, “HIGH SALT” and, where applicable, “HIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGE”. The font would be one point larger than the font used in the nutrition table on the back of the package. Bowing to corporate pressure? Supreme Court slams FSSAI's reluctance to put warning labels on foods high in sugar, salt, fat Under the proposal, the first phase would cover products high in at least two of the specified nutrients and certain sweetened beverages. The second phase would cover products high in any one of the nutrients. The Court acknowledged that “significant progress” has been made since its previous order but said several aspects of the proposal remained unclear. It questioned the basis for dividing the rollout into two phases, noting that sugar, salt and saturated fat could each be harmful independently. It also sought a fixed timeline between the phases, warning that the second phase could otherwise be indefinitely postponed. The Bench said consumer acceptability and the time required by the industry for reformulation could not, by themselves, justify uncertainty over when the second phase would be implemented. items.title: CCI rejects plea against Mahindra & Mahindra over warranty denial due to externally sourced engine oil
items.summary: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has dismissed a complaint accusing car manufacturer Mahindra & Mahindra and one of its authorised dealers of anti-competitive conduct for allegedly refusing warranty coverage because a vehicle owner used externally sourced engine oil. The CCI noted that the warranty agreement between Mahindra and the consumer contained a requirement that engine oil will be procured from Mahindra or its authorised dealers. Hence, the CCI held that the warranty terms agreed upon between the manufacturer and end consumer cannot be examined as a vertical restraint under Section 3(4) of the Competition Act. It also found no material to establish abuse of dominance under Section 4. It consequently held that the alleged requirement to procure engine oil from Mahindra or its authorised dealers, insofar as it formed part of the warranty arrangement with the consumer, fell outside the scope of Section 3 on anti-competitive agreements. The complaint was filed by one Bharti Sharma, who had purchased a Mahindra XUV700 vehicle from Delhi-based authorised dealer Sri Durga Automobiles in June 2024. She had also bought an extended warranty valid until July 2029. According to Sharma, she bought Pakelo Krypton XT LA-V SAE 5W-30 engine oil during scheduled services in January 2025 and January 2026. The dealer allegedly used the oil on both occasions without warning her that doing so could affect the warranty. Soon after the January 2026 service, the vehicle displayed a “check engine system” warning and suffered reduced acceleration. The dealer later diagnosed a defective turbocharger and gave an estimate of ₹50,000 for replacement and labour costs. However, Sharma alleged that her warranty claim was rejected because the engine oil had been procured externally. Mahindra subsequently told her that using externally sourced engine oil could invalidate warranty coverage. Sharma argued that the oil met Mahindra's specifications and accused the company of effectively forcing consumers to purchase lubricants through its authorised network. She claimed this restricted consumer choice and foreclosed competition in the aftermarket for lubricants and vehicle maintenance services. However, the CCI said the dispute essentially concerned warranty conditions applicable to Sharma's individual vehicle rather than a competition concern arising from abuse of market power. items.title: Religious conversion: Allahabad HC orders police to produce Ayush Malik after plea claims illegal detention by family
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed authorities in Uttar Pradesh to produce Ayush Malik before the Court on a plea alleging that he has been kept in illegal custody by his family after he converted to Islam and married a Muslim woman [Ayush Malik and Another v State of UP and 3 Others] Malik's conversion from Hinduism to Islam had led to the arrest of the Muslim woman Chandni Qureshi and her father under the Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021 in a case registered by Shamli police. Malik, who had changed his name to Mohammad Ali, had told the media that he had converted to Islam voluntarily. However, his businessman father claimed that he was coerced by the Muslim woman and her family to gain control over their property. Malik later reportedly returned to Hinduism. In a fresh twist to the story, a habeas corpus petition before the High Court states that Malik's father has deprived him of his personal liberty and kept him in illegal custody with the active assistance of the State machinery. The petition has been filed by one Sultan, who said he was Malik's friend. On September 9, Justice Sandeep Jain observed that Malik prime facie appeared to have voluntarily renounced Hinduism, embraced Islam and married the Muslim woman against the wishes of her father. Justice Sandeep Jain The Court said the allegations of his illegal custody warrant immediate consideration and directed the State and Malik's father to ensure his production before the Court on September 16. It added that in case Malik is not produced before the Court, the State authorities shall disclose the reasons for his non-production, and the steps taken by them to ensure his presence. "The allegations made by learned counsel for the petitioner regarding the alleged illegal detention of the corpus and the purported involvement of the State authorities and their functionaries in facilitating such detention are serious in nature and, therefore, warrant immediate consideration by this Court," the Court said. Advocates Deepak Singh, Mohammad Khalid and Umar Khalid represented the petitioner. items.title: Arbitration in India cannot deliver speed if hearings are months apart: SG Tushar Mehta
items.summary: Arbitration in India cannot deliver on its promise of speed if hearings are being fixed three, four or five months apart, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said on Thursday, while calling for arbitrators’ calendars to be checked before they are appointed. He said the purpose of arbitration was speed in dispute resolution, but crowded schedules of arbitrators were contributing to long gaps between hearings. He said he was impressed by an institutional model where an arbitrator’s calendar is sought before appointment. “ What happens is, in the absence of such a system in India, arbitrators are so busy that today there is an arbitration hearing; the next day to get this hearing will be after a few months, 3, 4, 5 months. That's the problem ,” Mehta said. SG Mehta was speaking during a fireside chat with Nish Shetty, Partner at Clifford Chance and Co-Chair of the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA) , on what India needs to do to make its arbitration system more effective and attractive to parties. The chat was organised at Convivium Artium - an Art Tour hosted by Chambers of Kunal Vajani as a part of India ADR Week 2026. Shetty asked what India needed to do to encourage parties from within and outside the country to have confidence that arbitrations in India would be conducted in a familiar and dependable manner. "I was really impressed by one model - one of the institutional models where, before appointing an arbitrator, his calendar is asked for," SG said. "There is a request for the calendar. And if the institution feels that his calendar permits conclusion of the arbitration within the statutorily fixed time, then only is he appointed." SG Mehta said India should consider adopting a similar mechanism. “ So we should incorporate institutional arbitration with a similar calendar appraisal system .” SG Mehta also backed a greater shift towards institutional arbitration over ad hoc arbitration. “If we concentrate more on institutional arbitration than individual arbitration, meaning that where the institution would choose the arbitrators and not the parties, then that might be a real boost in the arbitration.” The discussion also touched upon the relatively small share of institutional arbitration in India. items.title: Maharashtra anti-conversion law challenged before Bombay High Court
items.summary: AA petition has been filed before the principal bench of the Bombay High Court challenging the constitutional validity of the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026 . [Maulana Halimullah Farooque Ahemed Khan v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] The petition has been filed by 70-year-old Islamic scholar Maulana Halimullah Farooque Ahemed Khan. According to the plea, the newly enacted law infringes fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution. As per the plea, while prohibiting forced or fraudulent marriages is valid, such power cannot extend to state surveillance of consensual inter-faith relationships or voluntary religious conversions. “The choice of a life partner and the decision concerning one's faith constitute facets of personal autonomy, dignity, privacy and decisional freedom protected under Articles 21 and 25 of the Constitution,” the plea reads. Section 9(2) prescribes enhanced punishment for converting women. The plea terms this gender-discriminatory. The plea has also assailed Section 2(a) for defining "allurement" in vague, over broad terms. Phrases like "better lifestyle" and "divine healing" used in the provision would bar legitimate religious discourse and charity. As per the petition, “The threat of criminal proceedings, arrest, non-bailable prosecution, mandatory disclosure of personal information and public scrutiny under the impugned Act is capable of deterring individuals, religious organisations and institutions from undertaking legitimate religious teaching, preaching, charitable, humanitarian and related activities.” The plea has also challenged the mandatory 60-day notice before converting from one religion to another. The petition argues that this exposes personal faith choices to public scrutiny and state inquiry, violating privacy. “Where a person voluntarily chooses to change his or her religion, the constitutional inquiry must be confined to whether such decision was made freely, voluntarily and with full and informed consent; the State cannot legitimately investigate the individual’s beliefs, motivations or reasons for such choice merely because the person may have been exposed to religious instruction, persuasion or lawful charitable and humanitarian activities,” the petition states. items.title: Parties don't trust institutions yet: Mihir Thakore on why ad-hoc arbitration still wins in India
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) recently conducted a 3-day Arbitration Week 2026 at GIFT City Club, Gandhinagar The event brought together the judiciary, lawyers and arbitration practitioners to chart the future of institutional arbitration in India. On the sidelines of the event, Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja spoke with Senior Advocate Mihir Thakore on the state of Indian arbitration a decade after the 2015 amendments, the persistent trust deficit around institutional arbitration and why Ahmedabad's arbitration ambitions may struggle to move beyond the domestic market. Edited excerpts follow. [Watch Video] Pallavi Saluja (PS): Indian arbitration has undergone a significant change over the past decade. From your perspective, what has genuinely improved since the 2015 amendments and what reforms do we still need to make? Senior Advocate Mihir Thakore For arbitrations commenced after 2015, it still takes at least 3 years to conclude once pleadings are over, which is not a good sign. Mihir Thakore (MT): To some extent, there is an improvement in the timelines by which arbitration is getting over. I can’t say it's a huge improvement, but there is a marginal improvement. There is pressure from the arbitrator to finish the arbitration. Even so, for arbitrations commenced after 2015, it still takes at least 3 years to conclude once pleadings are over, which is not a good sign. I had a very good experience once. The arbitrator persuaded both parties that the matter turned purely on documents and that no evidence needed to be led, and both parties agreed. The matter was fixed for final hearing and the award came within 8 months. I completely agree with Mr (former Justice) Nariman on his last suggestion that there should be a regular appeal. There cannot be these half-hearted Section 34 applications. You’re wasting time; the district judge often doesn’t know how to deal with them. Instead, there should be a full-fledged appeal directly to a division bench of the High Court, nominated specifically for this purpose. That way, awards that are questionable on grounds of integrity can be tested before a division bench, which would serve the process better. items.title: CPI(M) reshuffles Kerala leadership after three successive poll drubbings
items.summary: The CPI(M) has made significant changes to its Kerala state secretariat and state committee, bringing in four new members to the secretariat and nine others to the state committee. The changes were decided at the party’s extended state committee meeting, an unusual exercise carried out outside the regular state conference process. The reshuffle comes after three successive electoral defeats for the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front in Kerala. The party lost the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the local body elections and the 2026 Assembly election, prompting an internal assessment of its organisational functioning and political approach. P Jayarajan from Kannur, V Sivankutty from Thiruvananthapuram and MB Rajesh from Palakkad have been inducted into the state secretariat. Rajya Sabha MP and journalist John Brittas will also function as part of the state secretariat in his capacity as an invitee to the CPI(M) Central Committee. The party's state secretariat will now have 20 members, including state secretary MV Govindan and former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. The other members are EP Jayarajan, KN Balagopal, P Rajeeve, KK Jayachandran, VN Vasavan, Saji Cherian, M Swaraj, PA Mohammed Riyas, PK Biju, Puthalath Dineshan, MV Jayarajan, CN Mohanan, P Jayarajan, V Sivankutty and MB Rajesh. KK Shailaja is also among the senior leaders in the state secretariat. The party has also decided to appoint P Rajeeve as the LDF convenor. At the same time, Central Committee members TM Thomas Isaac and TP Ramakrishnan have been removed from the state secretariat. Both Isaac and Ramakrishnan, as Central Committee members, can continue to participate in the state secretariat's proceedings. The party is describing the changes as an 'expansion' of the state secretariat and committee rather than a restructuring. The move is being viewed as part of the corrective measures discussed within the party following the electoral setbacks. items.title: 16 months in prison, still no trial for activist Rejaz Sydeek facing UAPA charges
items.summary: Nearly 16 months after his arrest, Kerala-based journalist and activist Rejaz M Sheeba Sydeek remains in prison without a trial in the UAPA case against him. Rejaz was arrested in Nagpur in May 2025 and later booked under the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) took over the investigation from the Nagpur Police, with other agencies, including the Kerala ATS, also looking into the case. The allegations against Rejaz centre largely on the claim by investigators that they have found allegedly incriminating material on his electronic devices and during a search of his residence in Ernakulam. Police have alleged that he had links with members of the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist) and other banned organisations. Among the material cited by investigators were conversations on Signal and Telegram, phone numbers allegedly belonging to people associated with banned organisations, and literature concerning the CPI (Maoist), Kashmir and armed groups. Police also claimed to have recovered several phones, pen drives, a hard drive, a memory card and other electronic devices from his home. Investigators had also questioned Rejaz's presence in Nagpur, a city with several sensitive security installations. Police said he had travelled there to meet a woman he had met on Instagram. They also cited photographs taken at a gun shop where the woman had photographed Rejaz holding an air rifle and a pistol. “It has been 500 days since he was jailed. There have been multiple hearings on his bail application, as well as on a petition seeking to discharge the chargesheet, before the District and Sessions Court in Nagpur. After several hearings on these petitions and repeated postponements, we have now been told that UAPA cases cannot be heard by that court. As a result, the proceedings are being delayed further. We have been actively campaigning to ensure that Rejaz gets bail,” said Hari, Convenor Janakeeya Manushyavakasha Prasthanam, a collective which is part of the group campaigning for Rejaz. A social media campaign demanding a fair trial and release of Rejaz was organised on September 13, which is observed as Political Prisoners Day in India to commemorate the martyrdom of Jatindra Nath Das, who died in prison after a 63-day-old hunger strike.

items.title: Tamil Nadu signs Rs 12,300 crore investment deals in UK, eyes 10,000 jobs
items.summary: Tamil Nadu has secured investment commitments worth Rs 12,300 crore during Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s first official visit to the United Kingdom. The agreements signed in London on Monday, September 14, cover advanced manufacturing, electrical and electronic equipment, and global capability centres. The projects are expected to create around 10,000 jobs in the state. The largest commitment came from Samvardhana Motherson International Limited and its European and UK-based joint venture companies, which signed an MoU for an investment of approximately Rs 11,000 crore. The investment is expected to generate around 7,000 jobs across design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and logistics facilities. The MoU was exchanged by Barrie Painter, global head of marketing and communications at Samvardhana Motherson International Group, and Deepak Jacob, managing director of Guidance Tamil Nadu. An additional Rs 1,000 crore investment is expected from an MoU with UK-headquartered Ernst & Young for establishing a Global Capability Centre in Chennai. The centre, proposed on Mount-Poonamallee Road, is expected to create more than 2,000 high-value jobs. Sweden-based Sigma Technology Group has also agreed to expand its existing GCCs in Chennai and Tiruchirappalli through its Indian entity, Zriya Solutions. The expansion is expected to create 600 high-value jobs in embedded systems, electrification and industrial digitalisation. UK-based Wilson Power Solutions signed another agreement involving an investment of Rs 300 crore in Tiruvallur district. The project is expected to create around 400 jobs and expand the state’s electrical equipment manufacturing capacity. A European automotive components manufacturer also submitted a Letter of Intent expressing its preference for Tamil Nadu as the location for a proposed Rs 3,000-crore investment in India. The state government has assured the company of support in setting up its operations. The MoUs are part of Vijay’s first official overseas visit since taking charge as Chief Minister. The state government had said the trip was aimed at attracting investments and strengthening Tamil Nadu’s existing business ties with the UK. The government is particularly seeking investments in advanced manufacturing, automobiles and electric vehicles, electronics and global capability centres. items.title: KTR’s aides allege attack by masked men inside police station in Hyderabad

Two of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao’s (KTR) aides have alleged that they were attacked by a group of masked men at the Saifabad police station on September 14, when they were called for questioning in a recent case against them. Khairatabad Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) K Shilpavalli has denied the allegation, stating that a group of men had gone to the station seeking permission for a Ganesh Chaturthi DJ event. “They argued with KTR’s aides and the police and left. The CCTV footage showed no assault,” she added in a statement to the media. Earlier on September 10, KTR’s Public Relations Officer (PRO) Manikya Mahesh and personal assistant Mahender Reddy were booked for allegedly abusing police officers on duty at the Telangana Assembly while the BRS was carrying out a protest against the Congress-led government. Following the FIR, the duo approached the Telangana High Court on September 11 to quash the FIR. While the FIR was not quashed, Justice J Sreenivasa Rao directed the police to continue the investigation without any coercive action against the two men. The police were also directed to not arrest either Mahesh or Mahender. However, both of them were called to the Saifabad police station on September 14 in connection with the investigation. Mahesh told TNM that a group of 25-30 men wearing masks attacked them in the station premises post which the men fled the station immediately. Mahesh alleged that Saifabad police had not accepted his complaint over the attack. “Our point is simple. If this can happen to KTR’s PRO or anyone in his team, then the situation is far more dire for a regular party member. Also this happened inside the interrogation room of a police station, not an ordinary public place. But the police didn’t register our FIR.” Mahesh also told TNM that they were called to the police station at 10 am and were made to stay there till 12 am in the night. “After the initial round of questioning, we were just made to wait for a few hours. We were told that they would let us go soon. The attack on us took place around 4 pm after which we were asked to stay until midnight,” he added. In a statement, KTR termed the attack “extremely heinous” and accused the Congress government of allowing a “rule of rowdies and goons” to prevail in Telangana. items.title: Bengaluru: Fake drugs sold to hospitals at discount, pharmacy owner arrested
items.summary: A Bengaluru Police Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the Drugs Control Department have uncovered a suspected counterfeit medicine racket that investigators believe supplied fake or repackaged drugs to more than 90 hospitals and clinics in the city. Pharmacy owner Veeresh Kumar Jain has been arrested in connection with the case. Police suspect his pharmacy, Krupa Healthcare near Minerva Circle, was being used to store and distribute the alleged counterfeit medicines. According to reports , Veeresh Kumar Jain is suspected to be part of a network that supplied counterfeit cancer medicines, other life-saving drugs, and ICU injections to hospitals, clinics and medical shops at discounts of around 50%. According to investigators, the racket allegedly involved procuring medicines at low prices, rebranding them and selling them under different names. Expired medicines were also allegedly repackaged in new containers and fitted with counterfeit labels, including labels resembling those of established pharmaceutical companies. The Krupa Healthcare premises is suspected to have served as a storage point before the medicines were distributed to medical shops, hospitals and clinics. Investigators are also examining the suspected involvement of more than 15 medical representatives in transporting or facilitating the distribution of the medicines. The investigation began after authorities seized suspected counterfeit medicines worth around Rs 5 crore during a raid at a farmhouse in the Bidadi and Dodderi areas of Bengaluru South district on August 18. Fake bills, injection-filling equipment, and counterfeit labels were also recovered. Following the seizure, the SIT widened its probe and conducted coordinated searches at more than 10 locations across Karnataka, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra. Investigators subsequently traced part of the suspected supply chain to Krupa Healthcare and Veeresh Kumar. Vamsi Krishna, Joint Commissioner of Police (West) and head of the SIT, told Indian Express that the investigation was still underway and the full extent of the suspected interstate network had not been established. “We have seized bank transaction records, purchase and sale vouchers, and other documents.
